strings.<p><strong>RCR, défibrillateur externe a:
CPR, Automated External Defibrillator (AED) and Choking Response

Become a vital link in the chain of survival.

Heart & Stroke’s Cardiac First Aid course teaches you how to recognise cardiac arrest and respond quickly using cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), an automated external defibrillator (AED) and techniques to clear a blocked airway.

No medical background is required. This course is for people who want to gain the essential skills needed to respond to emergencies, both at work and in everyday life.
strings.<p><strong>Une formation destinée aux pr:
Training for healthcare professionals

Heart & Stroke’s Immediate Resuscitation Care (SIR) course is designed for healthcare professionals who need to quickly recognise cardiac arrest and respond effectively, either on their own or as part of a resuscitation team.

Delivered entirely in person by a qualified instructor, this course combines theoretical learning, practical exercises and simulations to develop the skills needed to manage cardiopulmonary emergencies.

strings.<p>Une réaction allergique grave peut su:
A severe allergic reaction can occur within minutes. Recognise the signs: difficulty breathing, throat swelling, feeling faint or widespread hives. Administer epinephrine promptly using an auto-injector and call 911.

strings.<p>Chaque seconde compte lors d’un arrêt:
Every second counts during cardiac arrest. If someone is unconscious and not breathing normally, call 911, begin CPR and ask for an AED. Acting quickly can save a life.

General information. In an emergency, call 911 and follow the emergency responders’ instructions.
strings.<p>Un médicament qui peut renverser temp:

strings.<p>Fethi Boudebza est un formateur agréé:
Fethi Boudebza is an instructor certified by the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Canada. Certified since 2017, he has several years of experience in cardiopulmonary resuscitation and clinical training.

He has served as the Code Blue team leader at Douglas Hospital. He has also trained staff in CPR, first aid and responding to life-threatening emergencies. In addition, he provided CPR training to the nursing staff at the Philippe-Pinel Institute of Montreal.

As a specialised nurse practitioner (SNP), he also has clinical experience in acute care at the Jewish General Hospital. He has also taught nursing at Cégep André-Laurendeau.

His clinical and teaching experience enables him to provide thorough instruction focused on practical skills and tailored to participants’ needs.

strings.EPIPEN : <span style=\"white-space:nowra: EPIPEN: DO YOU KNOW HOW TO USE AN EPINEPHRINE AUTO-INJECTOR?
strings.<p>En situation d'anaphylaxie, savoir ut: In an anaphylactic emergency, knowing how to use an epinephrine auto-injector quickly is essential!
strings.<p>Un auto-injecteur comme EpiPen permet:
An auto-injector such as EpiPen allows epinephrine to be administered quickly during a severe allergic reaction.

Key steps:

  • Recognise the signs of an anaphylactic reaction.
  • Remove the device from its packaging and follow the manufacturer’s instructions.
  • Place the auto-injector against the outer thigh.
  • Activate the device according to the instructions for that specific model.
  • Call 911 immediately and follow the emergency responders’ instructions.

Remember: Do not delay the administration of epinephrine. A second dose may be needed, depending on the recommendations and applicable protocol.

💉 Practising with a trainer device helps build confidence and accuracy.

Learn how to use an epinephrine auto-injector correctly through our training!

strings.SURDOSE AUX OPIOÏDES : LA NALOXONE PEUT: OPIOID OVERDOSE: NALOXONE CAN SAVE A LIFE!
strings.<p>Saviez-vous que la naloxone peut temp: Did you know that naloxone can temporarily reverse the effects of an opioid overdose?
strings.<p>La naloxone est un médicament qui peu:
Naloxone is a medication that can temporarily restore the breathing of someone experiencing an opioid overdose.

How can you recognise a possible overdose?

  • The person is unconscious or difficult to wake.
  • Slow, irregular or absent breathing.
  • Unusual snoring or gurgling sounds.
  • Bluish or greyish lips or fingernails.

What to do:

  • Call 911 immediately.
  • Administer the available naloxone according to the device instructions.
  • Provide respiratory support and begin CPR if necessary, in accordance with your training.
  • If the person does not resume adequate breathing, administer another dose after 2 to 3 minutes, following the product instructions.
  • Stay with the person until emergency responders arrive.

⚠️ Naloxone may have a temporary effect. Monitoring and medical care remain essential.

Learn to recognise an overdose and administer naloxone. A quick response can save a life!

strings.<p>Une personne qui s'étouffe peut perdr: A person who is choking can quickly lose the ability to breathe. Do you know how to recognise an airway obstruction?
strings.<p><strong>Les signes à reconnaître :</s:
Signs to look for:

  • Difficulty speaking or inability to speak.
  • Ineffective or absent coughing.
  • Severe difficulty breathing.
  • Panic and, sometimes, bluish skin discolouration.

What should you do?

  • If the person is coughing effectively, encourage them to keep coughing.
  • If the obstruction is severe, use the appropriate airway-clearance techniques for the person’s age and condition.
  • If the person becomes unconscious, have someone call 911 and begin CPR in accordance with first-aid recommendations.

⚠️ Important: techniques differ for adults, children and infants.

Practical training helps you develop the right response skills so you can act without hesitation!
strings.RCR et DEA : chaque seconde compte: CPR and AED: every second counts
strings.<p>Saviez-vous qu'un arrêt cardiaque peu: Did you know that cardiac arrest can happen at any time, even to someone who appears to be in perfect health?
strings.<p>Lorsqu'une personne s'effondre, ne ré:
When someone collapses, becomes unresponsive and is not breathing normally, every second matters.

What to do:

  • Check that the scene is safe.
  • Check whether the person responds and is breathing normally.
  • Call 911 or ask someone else to call.
  • Start chest compressions immediately.
  • Ask for an AED and use it as soon as possible.

❤️ Did you know? Early CPR can significantly increase the chances of survival.

Learn how to respond: sign up for our CPR/AED training!

strings.<p>La réanimation cardiorespiratoire (RC: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a first-aid technique that helps maintain blood circulation and oxygen supply to the organs when someone is in cardiac arrest.
strings.<p>Lorsqu’une personne est inconsciente: When a person is unconscious and not breathing normally. Call 911 and begin CPR immediately, following your training and the dispatcher’s instructions.
strings.<p>Parce que le cerveau et les autres or: Because the brain and other organs are rapidly deprived of oxygen during cardiac arrest. A quick response increases the chances of survival.
strings.Peut-on pratiquer la RCR sans formation: Can CPR be performed without training?
strings.<p>Oui. Le répartiteur du 911 peut vous: Yes. The 911 dispatcher can guide you over the phone. However, practical training is recommended to develop the right response skills.
strings.<p>Un défibrillateur externe automatisé: An automated external defibrillator is a device that analyses the heart rhythm and determines whether an electric shock is needed.
strings.<p>Les DEA sont conçus pour être utilisé: AEDs are designed for use by the general public. The device provides simple voice instructions to guide the user.
strings.<p>Lorsqu’il est utilisé conformément à: When used according to its instructions, an AED is safe. Simply make sure no one touches the person during the analysis or while a shock is being delivered.
strings.Faut-il continuer la RCR après l’utilisa: Should CPR continue after using an AED?
strings.<p>Oui. Reprenez immédiatement la RCR lo: Yes. Resume CPR immediately when the device tells you to and continue until emergency responders arrive or the person shows signs of life.

strings.<p>Encouragez-la à continuer de tousser: Encourage them to keep coughing and monitor their condition. An effective cough may help dislodge the object.

strings.<p>Intervenez rapidement en appliquant l: Act quickly by applying airway-clearance techniques appropriate to the person’s age and condition, in accordance with your training and current recommendations.

strings.<p>L’anaphylaxie est une réaction allerg: Anaphylaxis is a severe and potentially life-threatening allergic reaction that requires immediate action.
strings.Quels sont les signes à reconnaître ?: What signs should you look for?
strings.<p>Les symptômes peuvent comprendre une: Symptoms may include difficulty breathing, swelling of the tongue or throat, hives, dizziness or a drop in blood pressure.
strings.<p>L’épinéphrine (adrénaline) est le tra: Epinephrine (adrenaline) is the first-line treatment. If anaphylaxis is suspected, it should be administered promptly using an auto-injector.

strings.<p>Oui. Même si la personne semble aller: Yes. Even if the person appears to be feeling better, urgent medical assessment is necessary.

strings.<p>L’EpiPen est un auto-injecteur qui pe: EpiPen is an auto-injector that delivers a dose of epinephrine quickly during a severe allergic reaction.

strings.Que faire après l’injection ?: What should you do after the injection?
strings.<p>Appelez le 911, surveillez la personn: Call 911, monitor the person and follow the emergency responders’ recommendations. A second dose may be needed depending on the situation and the medical or device instructions.
strings.<p>La naloxone est un médicament qui peu: Naloxone is a medication that can temporarily reverse the effects of an opioid overdose, including by helping restore breathing.

strings.<p>La personne peut être inconsciente ou: The person may be unconscious or difficult to wake, breathing very slowly or not at all, and may have very small pupils.

strings.<p>Appelez immédiatement le 911, adminis: Call 911 immediately, administer naloxone according to the device instructions, and provide breathing support or CPR in accordance with your training.
strings.<p>Non. Une dose supplémentaire peut êtr: No. An additional dose may be needed after 2 to 3 minutes if the person does not respond or symptoms persist, in accordance with the product instructions and applicable protocol.

strings.<p>Les soins immédiats en réanimation re: Immediate Resuscitation Care includes the essential interventions to perform when someone experiences a life-threatening emergency, particularly cardiac arrest.
strings.Quels sont les premiers gestes à poser ?: What are the first steps to take?
strings.<p>Vérifiez la sécurité des lieux, évalu: Check that the scene is safe, assess the person’s level of consciousness and breathing, ask for help and call 911. Begin the appropriate interventions in accordance with your training.
strings.<p>Parce qu’elle permet de reconnaître r: Because it helps you recognise an emergency quickly, respond with confidence and contribute to saving lives.
strings.La RCR est-elle différente chez l’enfant: Is CPR different for children and infants?
strings.<p>Oui. Les techniques, la profondeur de: Yes. The techniques, compression depth and certain steps differ depending on the person’s age and size.

strings.<p>Devenez un maillon fort de la chaîne: Become a vital link in the chain of survival.
strings.<p>La formation Cardio-secours de Cœur +:
Heart & Stroke’s Cardiac First Aid course teaches you how to recognise cardiac arrest and respond quickly using cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), an automated external defibrillator (AED) and techniques to clear a blocked airway.

No medical background is required. This course is for people who want to gain the essential skills needed to respond to emergencies, both at work and in everyday life.
strings.<p>Cette formation porte sur la RCR et l:
This course covers CPR and emergency response for adults.

It is particularly suitable for workplaces where emergencies mainly involve adults, including offices, retail businesses and certain industrial environments.
strings.Niveau C — Adulte, enfant et nourrisson: Level C — Adult, Child and Infant
strings.<p>Cette formation couvre les interventi:
This course covers emergency response for people of all ages: adults, children and infants.

It is particularly suitable for parents, childcare and school staff, sports coaches, and healthcare professionals who want to develop paediatric CPR skills.
strings.<p>La formation en soins immédiats en ré:
Heart & Stroke’s Immediate Resuscitation Care (SIR) course is designed for healthcare professionals who need to quickly recognise cardiac arrest and respond effectively, either on their own or as part of a resuscitation team.

Delivered entirely in person by a qualified instructor, this course combines theoretical learning, practical exercises and simulations to develop the skills needed to manage cardiopulmonary emergencies.
